text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident fired (INC-2057001234) -> service: redwood-api-prod (route: ops-primary)

pagerduty-bot: Trigger details: trigger_id=trg_9f3a, severity=high, alert: 502 spikes to customers, sample: 502 from edge -> upstream 504

jen_oncall: ack. I'm on it.

sam_m: wait — why did contractors group get paged? I just saw a PD notification that the escalation policy contains `contractor-oncall` as first responder.

maya_k: I can confirm. PD web shows `escalation_policy: api-route-main` -> binding order has `contractor-oncall` before `platform-oncall`. This looks wrong. :facepalm:

ben_r: paging log snippet: ```
2025-11-02T14:12:03Z incident created -> service: redwood-api-prod
2025-11-02T14:12:03Z routed to escalation_policy api-route-main
2025-11-02T14:12:03Z target: contractor-oncall (user_group: contractors-eng)
```

ops_bot: system note: recent schedule sync with HR rotation imported a shadow schedule named `contractors-temp` on 2025-11-01 03:00 UTC. It was auto-bound to `contractor-oncall` group.

jen_oncall: so a schedule import accidentally took precedence in the escalation policy binding? That can explain why the wrong responders got paged.

sam_m: we need to stop further pages to contractors ASAP — they don't have prod access.

ben_r: putting `redwood-api-prod` in PD maintenance mode now and removing contractor-oncall from the policy. cc @sre_lead for approvals.

sre_lead: approved. go for it.

ben_r: done. maintenance mode on, removed contractor-oncall from policy. rerouting to `platform-oncall`. PD update id=upd_7721.

pagerduty-bot: Update: maintenance mode enabled. New routing applied -> platform-oncall. Notifications suppressed to suppressed_targets: [contractor-oncall].

jen_oncall: ack, will take a look at the 502 spike. Initial triage: increased 502 rate around 14:10 UTC correlating with a rollout of routing config to edge (rollout id r-88ff). Rolling back that rollout now.

maya_k: customer impact: about ~120 requests/min failed for 6 minutes, affecting two tenants (acme.co, beta-saas). I've opened emergency support ticket SUP-1402 and DM'd customer-success.

sam_m: nice catch on the rollout. If rollback restores, we should unpause notifications and monitor.

jen_oncall: rollback completed at 14:20 UTC. error rate trending down. Will leave maintenance mode for 10m then lift.

ops_bot: note: created temporary incident bridge -> https://call.example.com/bridge/INC-2057001234

ben_r: root cause candidate: scheduled import merged a `contractors-temp` shadow schedule and a mistaken PD rule order. Two fixes: 1) revert schedule import job to ignore shadow schedules, 2) add validation to escalation policy bindings to prevent group precedence without prod-access tag.

sre_lead: agree. Assigning follow-up tasks: ENG-INC-543 = PD routing hardening, OWNER=ben_r; ENG-INC-544 = schedule-import hardening, OWNER=maya_k; ENG-INC-545 = customer-comms review, OWNER=sam_m.

jen_oncall: lifting maintenance mode now. Monitoring for 15m.

pagerduty-bot: Maintenance mode disabled. Notifications resumed.

maya_k: 14:36 UTC error rate is back to baseline. Customers trending green.

jen_oncall: incident closed for now. Will prepare short postmortem and action items. Thanks all, apologies to contractors who got woken up. :wave:

ben_r: quick note for postmortem: include PD audit log snippet and the `pdctl` commands we ran: ```
pdctl incidents update INC-2057001234 --maintenance on
pdctl escalation-policies update api-route-main --remove-target contractor-oncall
```

incident-bot: Incident INC-2057001234 marked RESOLVED by jen_oncall at 2057001299. Follow-up ticket ENG-INC-543 created.

sre_lead: follow-up: schedule a blast-radius test for PD routing rules in staging. Also add a runbook step for immediate maintenance-mode toggle.

sam_m: noted. I'll draft the postmortem and send to #postmortems with links to PD audit and the bridge logs.

jen_oncall: thanks everyone.
